chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī, from Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat over a جنازة, and pronounced five takbirs over him; and he performed salat over another, and pronounced four takbirs over him.

As for the one over whom he pronounced five takbirs, he praised Allah and glorified Him in the first takbir, and in the second he made du'a for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and in the third he made du'a for the believing men and believing women, and in the fourth he made du'a for the deceased, and he concluded at the fifth.

And as for the one over whom he pronounced four takbirs, he praised Allah and glorified Him in the first takbir, and in the second he made du'a for himself and the people of his household, and in the third he made du'a for the believing men and believing women, and he concluded at the fourth, and he did not make du'a for him because he was a hypocrite.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four takbirs in the funeral salat
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَةِ: a single pronouncement of takbir within the prayer
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person being prayed over
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ: the believing women for whom supplication is made
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believing men for whom supplication is made
key_terms.جِنَازَةٍ: a funeral bier or deceased person over whom funeral salat is performed
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five takbirs in the funeral salat
key_terms.مُنَافِقًا: a hypocrite, for whom du'a for the deceased was not made in this report

ai.seo_question: Why were five takbirs said over one deceased and four over another in the funeral salat?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in salat over the dead, showing different numbers of takbirs depending on the state of the deceased. It also outlines the order of praise and du'a within the funeral prayer, and indicates that du'a for the deceased was omitted in the case of a hypocrite.
